title: RTX's Raytheon doubling global Stinger missile production
summary: European production to boost output and strengthen the transatlantic defense industrial baseANKARA, Türkiye, July 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, is working with European companies, including Diehl Defence, to double Stinger® missile production in response to growing global demand.Working with Raytheon, Diehl Defence will produce the guidance section, a key component of the Stinger missile, and source related subcomponents from across Europe. Raytheon is also working with key Dutch suppliers to produce additional major Stinger assemblies. The final Stinger missile will be assembled, tested and completed in the Netherlands.
body_text: RTX's Raytheon doubling global Stinger missile production July 07, 2026 Share this article on Facebook Share this article on Twitter Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article via email European production to boost output and strengthen the transatlantic defense industrial base ANKARA, Türkiye , July 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Raytheon, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, is working with European companies, including Diehl Defence, to double Stinger® missile production in response to growing global demand. Working with Raytheon, Diehl Defence will produce the guidance section, a key component of the Stinger missile, and source related subcomponents from across Europe. Raytheon is also working with key Dutch suppliers to produce additional major Stinger assemblies. The final Stinger missile will be assembled, tested and completed in the Netherlands. "We are laser-focused on doubling our Stinger missile production capacity," said Tom Laliberty, president of Land & Air Defense Systems at Raytheon. "Expanding Stinger production in Europe strengthens our industrial base and broadens our global network, ensuring our allies have reliable access to this critical air defense capability." The Stinger missile is a lightweight, combat-proven and self-contained air defense system deployed by ground troops against cruise missiles and aircraft. Stinger is the preferred surface-to-air missile for 24 countries, including 10 NATO members. "We are proud to work together once again on Stinger, where we previously produced relevant parts of the missile," said Helmut Rauch, Diehl Defence CEO. "Producing the guidance section for new Stinger systems marks another strong chapter of cooperation between Diehl Defence and Raytheon." The expanded production capacity in Europe will help support future work with the NATO Support and Procurement Agency, known as the NSPA, to meet European demand. About Raytheon Raytheon, an RTX business, is a leading provider of defense solutions to help the U.S. government, our allies and partners defend their national sovereignty and ensure their security. For more than 100 years, Raytheon has developed new technologies and enhanced existing capabilities in integrated air and missile defense, smart weapons, missiles, advanced sensors and radars, interceptors, space-based systems, hypersonics and missile defense across land, air, sea and space. About RTX With more than 180,000 global employees, we push the limits of technology and science to redefine how we connect and protect our world. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defense systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia. For questions or to schedule an interview, please contact [email protected] About Diehl Defence As a reliable partner of the German and international armed forces, Diehl Defence is a leading system house for air defence systems. In addition to systems for ground-based air defence, the product portfolio of the company headquartered in Überlingen (Germany) includes guided missiles for all branches of the armed forces, ammunition for army, air force and navy as well as protection systems. In addition, Diehl Defence develops and produces key components such as infrared modules, fuzes and special batteries. Diehl Defence currently employs more than 6,000 people generating annual sales of over 2.5 billion euros. title: A European Energy Provider Transformed Its Technology Through an Integrated Customer Experience Management Platform
summary: Read how a renewable energy leader streamlined service and boosted satisfaction by transforming its customer experience management platform.
body_text: The client went on to implement a comprehensive transformation program aimed at overhauling its customer management processes. The heart of the solution was the integration of all functionalities into a single, cohesive platform: iX Hello™ All-In-One Customer Experience Management Platform This unified system not only streamlined the customer service process, but also empowered management with real-time data-driven decision-making capabilities. The iX Hello platform was designed to foster seamless connectivity between advisors and management, enhancing overall operational efficiency. Advisor Empowerment and Productivity By reimagining contact management through smart allocation and gamification, the client was able to keep advisors productive and engaged. The intuitive design of the portal minimized the complexity of actions advisors needed to perform, thus reducing training requirements and enabling them to deliver high-quality service confidently and efficiently. Innovation and New Opportunities The data-driven nature of the platform opened up new opportunities for the client to innovate and offer new energy products and services. This supported its goal of sustainable growth and assisted customers on their journey to net zero. Prior to implementation of the platform, advisors had to navigate multiple systems to resolve customer issues, leading to inefficiencies and a disjointed customer experience. Through the implementation of this platform, the client was able to achieve: Pre-emptive Resolution: Using data insights to help the client anticipate and proactively resolve issues before customers are aware. Intelligent Auto-Resolution: Enabling contact deflection, AI intervention, omnichannel self-service, and intelligent routing. Efficient Contact Resolution by Advisors: Providing advisors with tools (including AI) to empower them to take ownership of customer issues from start to resolution.

title: Isn't the Super Dislike supposed to hide stories?
summary: Maybe I understood wrong, question is basically the title. I have trained some stories with Super Dislike, but they still show up in my feed (with the small red dot on the left indicating they have tags I don’t like, which is still hard to see). Am I missing something? Thanks
body_text: SteveBuscemiDress July 20, 2026, 8:07am 1 Maybe I understood wrong, question is basically the title. I have trained some stories with Super Dislike, but they still show up in my feed (with the small red dot on the left indicating they have tags I don’t like, which is still hard to see). Am I missing something? Thanks 1 Like samuelclay July 21, 2026, 10:33pm 2 Thanks for the report. I took a look and your super dislikes are all saved correctly on your account, so this isn’t a case of them not sticking. They’re scoring the matching stories as hidden the way they should. So the question is where you’re seeing them. A super disliked story gets marked hidden, but hidden stories still show up in a couple of spots by design. On the web they appear if you’re in All Stories, or if you’ve clicked the “show hidden stories” bar above the story list. Switch to Unread or Focus and they drop out. If you trained them while the feed was already open, reload the feed so the change takes effect. On the iOS and Android apps, a story that was already loaded before you trained it won’t disappear on its own. Pull to refresh that feed so it rescores and they should go. Which platform are you seeing this on? If it’s Unread or Focus on the web and they’re still there after a reload, tell me and I’ll dig in from there. anon-37641789236 July 22, 2026, 1:24pm 3 I have this issue too, often. The posts have the red dot but show up in the feed. Best I can recall, this happens on iOS and not the web. Could it be because the training is applied before full-text is extracted? emm27 July 25, 2026, 5:18pm 4 I’m on iOS too and also see this frequently. I actually had started to think maybe Super Dislikes were a premium feature or something I just didn’t have access to. SteveBuscemiDress July 26, 2026, 12:16pm 5 Hello Samuel, thanks for the reply and sorry for my late response. I noticed this problem on Android, with the Newsblur app. I just made a quick test with one of my feeds, accessing it from the Android app and from the web. In the web, stories are correctly hidden whilst in Android, stories that should be hidden are shown (with the red dot on the left side that indicates they are disliked, but nonetheless they are shown). I trained the stories a long time ago so I believe it is not a problem of a story that was loaded before training. I’ll say the problem then is on the Android app side for the moment. title: Breaking Ground: New Sustainable Packaging Facility Coming to Mississippi
body_text: Last week, International Paper (NYSE: IP; LSE: IPC) celebrated the groundbreaking of its new sustainable packaging facility in Rankin County, Mississippi, marking a major milestone in the company’s strategic growth and long-term investment in the Mid-South region. Company leaders, state and local officials, customers, project stakeholders, and community partners gathered on Wednesday, May 20, in Brandon, Mississippi, to commemorate the start of the project, which will include construction of a new 468,000-square-foot corrugated packaging plant on an 80-acre site in the East Metro Center. The $225 million greenfield facility, located less than 10 miles from International Paper’s existing Richland box plant, will strengthen manufacturing and service capabilities across the Mid-South region. Designed to improve reliability, product quality, and cost position, the new facility supports growth in key market segments while reinforcing the company’s commitment to operational excellence, sustainability, and customer-focused innovation. Construction is expected to begin in June 2026, with operations anticipated in the fourth quarter of 2027. Employees at the existing Richland facility are expected to transition to the new plant upon completion. “This groundbreaking represents an important step forward for International Paper, our customers, and the communities we serve across the Mid-South,” said Keith Townsend, group vice president and general manager, IP North America Packaging Solutions East. “The Brandon facility will strengthen our manufacturing network with modern capabilities designed to improve safety, reliability, and operational performance, while positioning us to support long-term growth and deliver even greater value to our customers.” “This is another great day for Brandon, Rankin County, and Mississippi,” added Governor Tate Reeves. “Exactly two months ago, we announced International Paper’s $225 million investment. Today, we’re breaking ground on their new facility. It’s another example of Mississippi’s ‘insane execution speed’ and how much momentum our state has. When great companies want to move fast and build big, they come to Mississippi.”

title: Cafe Beacons debuts at Cannes Lions 2026
summary: Beacons is a free, all-in-one platform with the best link in bio, media kit builder, online store and email marketing tool for creators on Instagram + Tiktok
body_text: Cafe Beacons at Cannes Lions 2026: What Happens When an AI Teammate Shows Up in Real Life How a coffee stand on Creator Beach turned into Beacons' IRL introduction of our AI teammate to the creator economy — and what it means for the creators and brands who weren't there. Most of what creators and brands experience from an AI company is a login screen. A chat window. A product update in your inbox. Useful, probably efficient — but invisible in the way software tends to be invisible. You use it and move on. At Cannes Lions 2026, we made Beacons visible. We built a working cafe on Creator Beach — iced coffee, a growing pile of merch that people actually fought over, and Beam, our AI teammate, showing up as a character for the first time in his life. That bet — that the best way to build trust in an AI product is to get out from behind the screen — is what this activation was really about. Cafe Beacons was the experiment. Here's what we learned running it, and why we think it says something bigger about where the creator economy is headed in 2026. The bet: showing up in person at Cannes Lions 2026 Maybe building a coffee shop to promote our AI teammate wasn’t the most intuitive activation. But our team had a vision: Beacons helps creators run their business, so the most honest way to introduce it was to actually be useful and actually be there, in the middle of the one week a year when the entire creator economy sits on the same stretch of sand. Cafe Beacons ran daily during Cannes Lions, right at the entrance to Creator Beach. The Beacons team on the ground there quickly noticed the patterns in how visitors interacted: the coffee (iced coffee!) gave people a reason to come back more than once. Repeat visits turned into repeat conversations, and repeat conversations turned into ideas, next steps, and follow up calls. Making merch creators actually wanted to keep Our goal was to design Cafe Beacons like a lifestyle brand people would want to be seen wearing even after Cannes ended. The French Riviera inspired capsule — bucket hats, tote bags, paper fans, croissant-shaped charms, custom cup sleeves in a yellow you could spot from across the beach — was built for that job first. We wanted this to be the antithesis of boring corporate merch. It showed. The bucket hats sold out by day four, even with a shipping delay that kept them off the table on day one. The fans were gone by day three, useful enough in the Riviera heat that people wore them all week. The totes disappeared by the final day. The croissant charm turned into its own small phenomenon, with people coming back to grab more for friends and family members who weren’t there. And then there was Beam , Beacons’s AI teammate for creators. Bucket hat, croissant illustration, a very specific south-of-France vibe — he was the face of the whole activation. Midway through the week, a plush Beam briefly went missing from the café. What started as a shrug turned into a full narrative arc across our Stories and the founders' feeds: "BEAM HAS BEEN TAKEN," with people tracking the saga and stopping by the café daily for updates. The team embraced the spontaneous moments and opportunities for content that came from building a character people cared about. What we heard about the creator economy The conversations were the real product of the week, and a few of them will shape what we build next. A session with L'Oréal and Meta shared data showing AI-assisted creator selection driving nearly 2x the brand lift of standard benchmarks, with micro and nano creators now accounting for close to half of total influencer impact. The industry is aligned with what Beacons has been building. Zoom out from our café, and the same themes were echoing across the entire festival — probably the closest thing to a set of Cannes Lions 2026 creator marketing takeaways you'll find in one place. More than 250 creators showed up across official Cannes Lions programming this year, the most in the festival's history, and the dedicated creator track moved out of a side venue into the main festival footprint, sitting alongside the brand marketers and platform leads for the first time. The industry's own framing shifted too, from talking about what AI could eventually do to talking about what it's actually delivering right now. The Lions winners this year leaned into creators as strategic partners with real equity in the outcome. And more than one recap of the week landed on the same idea: as AI becomes part of the daily texture of work, trust and human connection turn into the scarce, valuable thing. That's the bet Cafe Beacons made, too. Why this matters beyond Cannes Lions 2026 Here's the thread tying all of it together, and it's the reason we're already planning for 2027. We believe AI companies are going to compete on the world built around their product — the community, the taste, the real-world moments that make a platform feel like a place you belong. Cafe Beacons was our first real rep at building that, and we're already planning the next one. Beam met a lot of people for the first time this week, as a character that exists even beyond the product. The introduction that actually matters is this: Beam is the AI teammate built into Beacons , built to run the parts of your creator business that shouldn't eat your whole week — content, outreach, brand deals, the operational stuff that gets in the way of the actual creative work. If you're a creator: this is your invitation to meet Beam properly. Sign up for Beacons and put an AI teammate to work on the busywork of running your business, inside the same all-in-one platform creators are already using to manage their links, their media kits , and their brand relationships in one place. If you're a brand: the creators we met on Creator Beach are exactly who you're trying to reach — real operators, media-kit-ready, already building audiences AI can't fake. Beacons for Brands is where you find and build campaigns with them directly, without the layers a traditional agency adds in between. We'll see you at the next cafe - make sure to follow us @beacons.ai to find it!

title: Best Serums for Post-Acne Dark Marks (PIH) in 2026
summary: The best serum for post-acne dark marks pairs tranexamic and azelaic acids with niacinamide to fade post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. See 6 ranked picks.
body_text: The breakout heals, but the brown mark it leaves behind can linger for months. The right serum can speed that fading — if it targets pigment, not just texture. Quick Answer The best serum for post-acne dark marks is a leave-on formula that pairs pigment-blocking actives — tranexamic acid, azelaic acid, and niacinamide — with gentle exfoliating acids to clear excess melanin faster. Post-acne marks are post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH): flat brown or gray spots left after a blemish heals, not raised or indented scars. Our top pick is Lion Pose's UNSPOTTED 4X Acid Jelly Night Serum (~$79), which combines tranexamic acid, azelaic acid, glycolic and lactic acids, niacinamide, and glutathione in one nightly step. Pair any of these serums with daily sunscreen, since UV exposure deepens dark marks and slows fading. What Are Post-Acne Dark Marks (PIH)? Post-acne dark marks are post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH) — patches of excess melanin the skin produces in response to the inflammation of a pimple. When a breakout triggers inflammation, melanocytes overproduce pigment, which stays behind as a flat brown, tan, or gray spot after the blemish itself has cleared. Because this is a pigment problem and not a wound, PIH is not permanent; it fades as the skin sheds and remodels that extra melanin, per dermatology references like StatPearls . The distinction matters for treatment. Epidermal PIH — pigment near the skin's surface — looks tan to dark brown and responds well to topical serums. Dermal PIH sits deeper, appears blue-gray, and is more stubborn, sometimes needing in-office treatment. Are Dark Marks the Same as Acne Scars? No — post-acne dark marks are flat pigment, while true acne scars are changes in skin texture, and serums treat only the first. PIH is a color change: a brown or gray spot you could not feel with your eyes closed. Atrophic scars (icepick, boxcar, rolling) are indentations where collagen was lost, and raised scars are excess tissue; both are structural and generally need procedures like microneedling, lasers, or fillers rather than a serum. There's a third look-alike worth naming: post-inflammatory erythema (PIE), the flat pink or red marks acne can leave, especially on lighter skin. PIE is a vascular change rather than pigment, so pigment-fading serums help it less than color-neutral healing and sun protection do. If your marks are brown, a dark-spot serum is the right tool; if they're indented, see a dermatologist about resurfacing. What Ingredients Fade Post-Acne Marks Fastest? The most effective serums combine a tyrosinase-inhibiting brightener with a melanin-transfer blocker and a gentle exfoliant. Tranexamic acid interrupts the pathway that links inflammation and UV exposure to pigment production, and one 2024 study in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology found a tranexamic-acid, niacinamide, and acetyl-glucosamine serum visibly improved PIH and post-acne marks across a diverse group of skin tones. Azelaic acid inhibits the tyrosinase enzyme melanocytes use to make pigment and calms the acne-related inflammation that causes marks in the first place, which is why dermatologists reach for it often for post-acne discoloration. Niacinamide works differently — it reduces the transfer of finished pigment from melanocytes into surface skin cells — so pairing it with tyrosinase inhibitors covers two steps of pigment formation at once. Rounding out a strong formula, alpha-hydroxy acids (glycolic and lactic) speed cell turnover so pigmented cells shed sooner, and antioxidants like vitamin C and glutathione help limit new pigment triggered by daily oxidative stress. How Long Do Post-Acne Dark Marks Take to Fade? Epidermal post-acne marks typically fade over 6 to 12 months on their own, and a well-formulated serum plus daily sunscreen can meaningfully shorten that. Left untreated, PIH can take months to years to resolve, according to StatPearls and clinical sources compiled by LearnSkin . Consistency is what drives results: most brightening actives need 8 to 12 weeks of nightly use before the difference is obvious. The single biggest accelerator — or saboteur — is sun exposure. Ultraviolet light re-stimulates the same melanocytes that made the mark, so skipping sunscreen can undo weeks of progress. Broad-spectrum SPF every morning is a non-negotiable part of any dark-mark routine, not an optional add-on. Do Post-Acne Marks Differ on Darker Skin Tones? Yes — post-acne marks are more common, more intense, and longer-lasting on deeper skin tones. People with Fitzpatrick skin types III to VI have more reactive melanocytes and a higher baseline of melanin, so inflammation from acne triggers pigment more readily; incidence of PIH reaches as high as 65% among people with darker skin and acne, per StatPearls . This is also why gentleness matters: harsh, irritating products can spark fresh inflammation and, ironically, new dark marks. For richer skin tones, the winning approach is steady, low-irritation brightening — tranexamic acid, azelaic acid, and niacinamide are well suited because they fade pigment without the sensitizing risk of high-strength peels. The American Academy of Dermatology's guidance on fading dark spots likewise stresses patience and daily sun protection over aggressive treatments. Lion Pose's UNSPOTTED leads because it bundles the whole evidence-backed pigment-fading toolkit into one nightly jelly: tranexamic acid and azelaic acid to block new pigment, niacinamide to stop pigment transfer, glycolic and lactic acids to resurface, and glutathione as an antioxidant backstop. It's built for flat brown post-acne marks and uneven tone, and the acids do double duty on the rough, dull texture marks often come with. Honest caveat: it fades pigment and smooths surface texture, but it won't fill indented (atrophic) scars — those need in-office resurfacing. Use it at night and always follow with morning SPF. SkinMedica Lytera 2.0 — ~$154. A pigment-correcting serum well regarded for stubborn, long-standing discoloration, layering tranexamic acid and niacinamide with brightening phytoactives. It's a strong option if cheaper serums haven't moved the needle — the main caveat is the premium price. SkinCeuticals Discoloration Defense — ~$115. This serum is purpose-built for post-inflammatory discoloration, combining 3% tranexamic acid, 1% kojic acid, 5% niacinamide, and HEPES to lift dull surface cells. It's a focused, elegant formula; the trade-off is cost relative to the drugstore options below. Topicals Faded Serum — ~$38. A popular pick for post-blemish marks, blending kojic acid, niacinamide, azelaic acid, and tranexamic acid, and frequently recommended for deeper skin tones. It's a well-rounded mid-price choice; sensitive skin should patch-test first. Naturium Tranexamic Topical Acid 5% — ~$22. A budget-friendly multi-brightener pairing 5% tranexamic acid with kojic acid, niacinamide, and licorice root. It's a smart entry point for fading marks without spending much, though results ask for patience and consistency. The Ordinary Azelaic Acid Suspension 10% — ~$12. The gentlest, most affordable way to add azelaic acid to a routine, suited to sensitive or acne-prone skin and often chosen by those avoiding stronger actives. It works on tone and marks slowly; think of it as a starter or a companion rather than a one-step fix. Prices are approximate and current as of July 21, 2026; check each retailer for the latest. Frequently Asked Questions Can you fade post-acne marks without a dermatologist? Yes, most flat post-acne marks (PIH) fade with a consistent over-the-counter routine: a brightening serum with tranexamic acid, azelaic acid, or niacinamide at night, plus daily sunscreen. See a dermatologist if marks are indented, blue-gray and deep, or unchanged after three to four months of steady use. Does sunscreen really help post-acne marks? Yes — daily broad-spectrum sunscreen is one of the most important steps for fading post-acne marks. Ultraviolet light re-triggers the melanocytes that created the dark spot, deepening it and slowing recovery. Wearing SPF 30 or higher every morning protects the progress your serum makes and helps prevent new marks from forming. Can I use a dark-spot serum while I still have active acne? Often yes, but choose gentle actives and go slowly. Azelaic acid and niacinamide treat active acne and fade marks at once, making them ideal during breakouts. Stronger acids or layering several products can irritate inflamed skin and cause more marks, so introduce one product at a time and patch-test first. Are post-acne dark marks permanent? Most post-acne dark marks are not permanent. Epidermal PIH, the common tan-to-brown kind, typically fades over 6 to 12 months and faster with treatment. Deeper dermal PIH, which looks blue-gray, is more stubborn and may need professional treatment. True indented scars are structural and won't fade on their own. Is azelaic acid or tranexamic acid better for post-acne marks? Both work well, and using them together is often best. Azelaic acid calms acne inflammation while blocking pigment, making it ideal when breakouts are still active. Tranexamic acid targets the UV-and-inflammation pathway that drives marks. Serums that combine them, like UNSPOTTED, cover more of the pigment process than either active alone. The Bottom Line Post-acne dark marks are pigment, not permanent damage, which is exactly why the right serum can help them fade faster than time alone. Look for a formula that attacks pigment from several angles — tranexamic and azelaic acids to block it, niacinamide to move it out, and gentle acids to turn skin over — then give it a consistent 8-to-12-week run and protect it with daily sunscreen. If you want that full toolkit in one nightly step, UNSPOTTED 4X Acid Jelly Night Serum is the simplest place to start. Whatever you choose, the marks you're seeing now are on their way out — steady treatment and sun protection just help them leave sooner. This article is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice. If your dark marks are deep, spreading, or not improving, or if you're unsure whether they're pigment or scarring, consult a board-certified dermatologist.
